note: Registered cell expectations for Study 016, locked-replication stratum, revised at review round 1 (see PREREG-REVIEW.md; matrixVersion 1 is the pre-review draft). Layers: owp = openworkproof.acceptance.verify_acceptance_bundle unchanged, run by Study 014's frozen adapter; binding = Study 014 adapter Layer BINDING; replay = Study 014 adapter Layer REPLAY; currency = this study's Layer CURRENCY (registry/SPEC.md section 3). Expected values are adjudicated layer OUTCOME strings and nothing else: 'pass', 'fail' (owp only - upstream reports one composite verdict), 'fail:<code>' with an exact registered code, or 'unavailable' (on the currency layer definitionally the pair verdict=unavailable, code=currency-unavailable). combined is derived: pass iff every layer outcome is pass. Roles: endpoint rows decide R1; control-gate rows are validity gates evaluated first; demonstration and descriptive rows are published, never counted. registeredUndetected: true marks cells whose all-pass outcome is itself the registered finding - on an endpoint a detection there is a divergence that falsifies R1 (decision D-3, now scoped to cur-split-view-a alone; cur-workorder-remint-accepted is descriptive per 014's e22 precedent and round-1 finding R1-2). attackerCapability: none = no key and no signed byte touched; tamper = signed bytes changed without re-signing; authority-key = the registry authority's own key signs the construction (the single-operator threat); full-keys = an insider holding every chain fixture key. variant: registry = only the registry snapshot varies from pos-current; config = only the trust configuration varies; chain = a different flowed chain; artifact = a retained artifact edited, nothing signed touched; tampered = signed bytes changed without re-signing; resigned = rebuilt validly with fixture keys; none = the untouched positive composition. identityGroups registers deliberate byte-identity: every cell file in a group is byte-identical across the group's members, verified by the scorer - the audit-vs-reuse indistinguishability exhibit is this identity, not a separate construction. pairs.split-view names the fork exhibit: the scorer validates the fork STRUCTURALLY from the two cells' snapshot bytes (same pinned genesis record, same authority key id, same attested position, different heads) and derives the pair report from the adjudicated outcomes; nothing is hardcoded (round-1 R1-4).

cells.construction: baseline chain; the position-2 snapshot [add 0.1.0, add 0.2.0] - both versions current; no minimum head pin
cells.note: one adjudication, two registered readings (round-1 R1-9): (1) membership in a concurrent supported set - never latest-version arithmetic (RFC 0011 R-8); (2) the freshness-floor reading, ANALYTIC and not separately scored: these bytes are also exactly what a verifier holding no minimum head pin would see if a newer retiring snapshot were withheld - the bytes carry no evidence either way, which is the registered indistinguishability, not an empirical withholding detection. The design point's other arm is cur-older-snapshot-pinned

cells.construction: baseline chain; registry [add 0.1.0, retire 0.1.0, reinstate 0.1.0] at position 3
cells.note: an authorized reinstatement is a signed lifecycle event, distinguished from a prefix rewrite by signature and head-consistency, not version arithmetic. reinstate is the ONLY re-entry event: a re-add of a bound version is refused (round-1 R1-13)

cells.note: never-registered is not retired (decision D-4): a registry that answers nothing for the pinned series is an empty answer, distinct from a retirement and from a chain defect. The two trust roots are both registered; the one-genesis-serves-the-matrix claim from the draft is withdrawn

cells.construction: Study 014's e22 construction rebuilt under this study's replay tuple: the identical judgment commitment re-bound under a different, equally valid work order; registry has 0.1.0 current

Its all-pass outcome is published as the registered scope boundary; authorization-contract currency belongs to the receipt protocol

cells.construction: one authority, one pinned genesis, continuation A: [genesis add 0.1.0, add 0.2.0] - internally valid; the fresh verifier holds only its per-series pins and no minimum head pin
cells.note: the load-bearing exhibit, half A: this view verifies clean. What is registered impossible is detection by a FRESH, STATELESS, two-pin verifier given exactly one view (round-1 R1-4 narrowed wording) - not by every offline verifier: the stateful arm below refuses the sibling. The scorer validates the fork structurally from bytes

cells.construction: the same authority and genesis, continuation B: [genesis add 0.1.0, retire 0.1.0] - equally valid, contradicting A at the same position
cells.note: half B: the same chain reads not-current under this view. Each verdict is internally correct; the equivocation lives only across the pair, which no single fresh stateless run can observe

cells.construction: view B presented to a verifier provisioned with view A's position-2 head as its minimum head pin - the state a sequential verifier that had accepted A would have persisted (round-1 R1-4/R1-5)
cells.note: the arm that bounds the split-view finding: prior-acceptance state converts the silent fork into a refusal by prefix containment (same length, different head). The fresh-verifier silence in the pair is exactly statelessness, and cross-verifier comparison or witnessing - out of the registered trust model - is what the transparency-log direction would add

cells.construction: the position-2 prefix snapshot of the retiring history (byte-identical snapshot to cur-concurrent-set's) presented to a verifier provisioned with the position-3 head as its minimum head pin
cells.note: the design point, decided against its sibling reading on cur-concurrent-set: the identical presentation is refused if and only if the verifier holds prior-acceptance state. The pin is caller-provisioned, registered as the state a production verifier would persist (round-1 R1-5: this layer holds no storage and returns no state update - a durable high-water lifecycle is future work, not claimed)

cells.construction: a fresh verifier with the series and authority key pinned but no genesis head; the registry itself is the valid current one
cells.note: the two-pin minimum: below a pinned genesis the verifier is trust-on-first-use and must refuse to call anything current - fail-closed, never a pass, never a detection

cells.note: disclosed designed demonstration (m28 convention), published and never counted: the scenario label lives only in this registry entry - no retained byte differs from dem-freshness-stale, so the verdict provably cannot carry the distinction (RFC 0011 R-7)

cells.construction: byte-copy of cur-retired-reuse; scenario: the decision is genuinely reused after 0.1.0 retired
